topStories.headline: ASNA Chronicles Over a Decade of Community-Funded Tree Planting at Alamo Square Park
topStories.dek: A September 30 post by the Alamo Square Neighborhood Association documents the full arc of its 'Trees for Future Generations' reforestation program — more than 147 trees planted, $100,000 raised, and another phase planned through 2028.
topStories.body:
The Alamo Square Neighborhood Association published a detailed account of its long-running reforestation program on September 30, tracing the effort from a 2011 horticultural assessment through multiple planting phases that have reshaped the park's urban canopy. The post, titled "Did you know ASNA buys trees for Alamo Square Park?", documents why a neighborhood organization took on work that is typically a city function — and why it plans to keep going.

The story starts with a professional HortScience Report ASNA commissioned in 2011, which found 166 trees across 21 species, an aging canopy in active decline, and a clear recommendation for a structured, long-term replanting program. Between 2010 and 2015, roughly 60 trees were lost to drought, wind, and storm damage. ASNA responded by developing a Forestation Plan with TS Studio landscape architects and launching a matching fundraising campaign, ultimately raising more than $100,000 alongside community donors.

Over subsequent years, 147 new trees representing more than 20 species were planted at the park. Of those, 63 trees in 5- and 15-gallon sizes were installed by SF Recreation and Park, while 74 larger trees in 24-inch boxes were planted by a contractor funded directly by ASNA. The planting program has introduced drought-tolerant, species-diverse stock intended to outlast the aging cypress-heavy canopy it is replacing.

ASNA's post notes that the next phase of the program is planned to continue through 2028, focusing on targeted replacement plantings to address trees lost to storms and other environmental stressors. SF Recreation and Park has historically lacked the budget for this kind of sustained replanting, making the neighborhood association's role unusual and, by its own account, far from finished.

topStories.headline: Hayes Street Is Now Closed Twice a Week — and a Noncompliance Counter Sits at 87 Weeks
topStories.dek: With the new Hayes Valley Farmers Market running Saturday mornings alongside the existing Shared Spaces permit, the 400 block of Hayes is car-free on Friday evenings and all day Saturday through at least year-end — and a neighborhood watchdog says permit violations have gone unaddressed for nearly two years.
topStories.body:
The SFMTA confirmed in an October 2026 travel advisory that Hayes Street between Gough and Octavia will remain closed to vehicles every Friday from 4 to 10 p.m. and every Saturday from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. through the remainder of the year. The agency is rerouting the outbound 6 Hayes/Parnassus Muni line around the area during closure hours, with the advisory page noting updates will continue monthly.

The two-layer closure reflects two separate permits operating simultaneously on the same block. The original Shared Spaces permit covers Friday evenings and Saturday programming. A separate Farmers Market permit — approved by SFMTA's ISCOTT committee on April 23, 2026, and treated as a standalone "special event" without coordinated review of the underlying Shared Spaces permit — added a year-long weekly Saturday morning market managed by the Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association.

Neighborhood watchdog group HVSafe, which has filed formal administrative complaints with SFMTA, published an August 2026 update putting the documented-noncompliance count at 87 consecutive weeks. Conditions their monitors have repeatedly flagged include vehicles parked inside the closure footprint during operational hours, absent barricade management, and unauthorized vendor activity. In published analysis, HVSafe estimated direct costs to SFMTA and San Francisco taxpayers at well over $100,000 per year — for a program the group says the agency, which faces a $307–322 million budget deficit, continues to subsidize without substantive corrective action.

The Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association and Hayes Promenade have defended the closure as a community asset that draws neighbors and local commerce to the block on weekends. SFMTA's October advisory makes clear the current arrangement will run through at least December 2026.

topStories.headline: Alamo Scare! Returns October 25 with a New Costume Swap at the Painted Ladies
topStories.dek: The Alamo Square Neighborhood Association's annual free Halloween block party is back on Sunday, October 25, with Strange Exchange joining for the first time to host a community costume exchange alongside the traditional trick-or-treat.
topStories.body:
The Alamo Square Neighborhood Association announced on September 6 that its Alamo Scare! block party will return on Sunday, October 25, from 4 to 6 p.m., with Steiner Street between Hayes and Grove closed to traffic in front of the Painted Ladies. The free, family-friendly event has grown into one of the neighborhood's most anticipated autumn traditions, drawing hundreds of costumed children and families each year to trick-or-treat at the historic Victorian row houses.

New this year: Strange Exchange, a community swap project at strangeexchangesf.org, will join the festivities to host a costume exchange. Residents can bring last year's costumes and pick out something for this year. Strange Exchange is also accepting candy buckets and Halloween decorations. Donation drop-offs are available on Sundays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. throughout October at the Divisadero Farmers Market in the DMV parking lot at 1377 Fell Street.

ASNA is also calling for volunteers to help run the event. Those interested can sign up through a form linked on the ASNA website at alamosquare.org. The event is free to attend and open to all ages.

events.title: Fleet Week Brass Band Concert at Patricia's Green
events.location: Patricia's Green, 489 Hayes Street, Hayes Valley
events.description: The 1st Marine Division Brass Band performs a free outdoor lunchtime concert at Patricia's Green as part of San Francisco Fleet Week 2026. No tickets required.

events.title: PROXY Fall Film Fest 2026: I Love Boosters
events.description: Boots Riley's 2026 film I Love Boosters — a fashion-forward mayhem extravaganza about professional shoplifters targeting a cutthroat fashion maven — screens free and outdoors. Beverages from Fort Point Beer, Fig & Thistle, and Millay sake bar available for purchase.

events.title: Flamekeeper Workshop: Designing Everyday Rituals for Extraordinary Times
events.location: The Commons, 550 Laguna Street, Hayes Valley
events.description: A community workshop on building intentional daily rituals, hosted at The Commons in Hayes Valley. See hayesvalleysf.org for registration details.

events.title: PROXY Fall Film Fest 2026: Hoppers
events.description: Daniel Chong's 2026 animated film Hoppers — in which wildlife lover Mabel hops human consciousness into lifelike robotic animals to uncover mysteries of the animal world — screens free outdoors at PROXY. All beverage proceeds support free outdoor cinema.

events.title: PawSpace Pup Up Marketplace Block Party
events.description: PawSpace Foundation presents a dog-friendly outdoor marketplace block party in Hayes Valley with vendors and community activities. Listed on the Hayes Promenade events calendar.

events.title: PROXY Fall Film Fest 2026: One Battle After Another
events.description: The final screening of PROXY's 2026 Fall Film Festival features One Battle After Another, described as an epic revolutionary tale. Free and open to all; beverages available for purchase to support the free cinema program.

events.title: Alamo Scare! Trick-or-Treat at the Painted Ladies
events.location: Steiner Street between Hayes and Grove, Alamo Square
events.description: ASNA's annual free Halloween block party closes Steiner Street in front of the Painted Ladies for trick-or-treating, music, costumes, and candy. This year Strange Exchange joins to host a community costume swap — bring last year's costume, leave with a new one.

events.title: Hayes Valley Farmers' Market
events.description: The Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association operates a weekly certified farmers market on the Hayes Street Promenade every Saturday. Launched June 6, 2026; runs through December 26.

moreNews.headline: ASNA General Meeting Took Place October 6 at The Archbishop's Mansion
moreNews.body: The Alamo Square Neighborhood Association held its October general meeting on Tuesday, October 6, at The Archbishop's Mansion, 1000 Fulton Street. The next scheduled gathering is a board meeting on November 10 at the same location, from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Residents can find agendas and details at alamosquare.org.

moreNews.headline: Weekly Hayes Valley Neighborhood Cleanup Continues Every Saturday Through December 26
moreNews.body: Organized by the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association in partnership with the Civic Joy Fund, SF Public Works, and several community groups, the Hayes Valley Community Cleanup runs every Saturday from 10 to 11 a.m. through December 26. Volunteers gather at Gambit Lounge, 581 Hayes Street, and receive vouchers for discounts at local merchants after each session.

restaurants.name: Rich Table
restaurants.description: Husband-and-wife chefs Evan and Sarah Rich serve hyper-seasonal, inventive California cuisine in a lively Hayes Valley dining room — one of SF's toughest reservations since 2012.

restaurants.name: RT Bistro
restaurants.description: The more casual, 37-seat sister spot to Rich Table — opened early 2026 next door — featuring the RT Bistro burger, one-layer lasagna, and a crowd-pleasing bistro menu.

restaurants.name: RT Rotisserie
restaurants.description: The Rich Table team's fast-casual offshoot focused on rotisserie chicken and home-style seasonal dishes, open daily in Hayes Valley.

restaurants.name: Nightbird

restaurants.name: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar

restaurants.name: Zuni Café
restaurants.description: A San Francisco institution since 1979, Zuni occupies a triangular Market Street building and is legendary for its wood-fired roast chicken and brick-oven cooking.

restaurants.name: Suppenküche
restaurants.description: Hayes Valley's beloved Bavarian Wirthaus since 1993, offering hearty German classics like schnitzel, pretzels, and an exceptional specialty beer list.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Home
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand-recognized Hayes Valley spot serving hand-folded xiao long bao (soup dumplings), pan-fried buns, and other Chinese classics.

restaurants.name: Hazie's
restaurants.description: A stylish Hayes Valley restaurant praised for its cocktails, happy hour, and modern American dinner menu in a comfortable neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Souvla
restaurants.description: The original Hayes Valley location of this beloved Greek fast-casual chain, known for rotisserie meats, big salads, and a sunny backyard patio.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman West
restaurants.description: A cozy Hayes Valley French bistro serving classics like steak frites, mussels, and crêpes in a lively street-side setting.

restaurants.name: Smuggler's Cove
restaurants.description: A three-story Hayes Valley tiki bar with more than 1,300 varieties of rum — the largest selection of any bar in the US — and a 80-cocktail menu of tiki classics and originals.

restaurants.name: Nopa
restaurants.description: The neighborhood namesake at 560 Divisadero has served organic wood-fired California cuisine with a daily-changing menu since 2006, remaining one of SF's most beloved dining rooms.

restaurants.name: Bar Crudo
restaurants.description: A vibrant NoPa raw bar specializing in creative crudo, fresh oysters, and sustainably sourced seafood, with a popular happy hour running Monday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Horsefeather
restaurants.type: Cocktail bar and New American restaurant
restaurants.description: A reliably good NoPa cocktail bar and restaurant with inventive drinks, fried chicken, duck fat fries, and a warm Arts-and-Crafts-inspired interior open late nightly.

restaurants.name: Brenda's Meat & Three
restaurants.description: New Orleans–born chef Brenda Buenviaje's NoPa diner lets diners choose one meat and three sides from a rotating array of down-home Southern classics, with a legendary breakfast menu.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Chef Gonzalo Guzmán's original Broderick Street location — open since 2009 — serving blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and seasonal Mexican dishes rooted in Veracruz family cooking.

restaurants.name: Altamirano Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A spacious NoPa Peruvian restaurant with an exhibition kitchen, a lively bar, and an outdoor courtyard with a fire pit for dining al fresco.

hotels.name: Hayes Valley Inn
hotels.description: A well-located, affordable 2-star inn on Gough Street in the heart of Hayes Valley, offering easy access to the neighborhood's restaurants, shops, and performing arts venues.

hotels.name: The Grove Inn
hotels.description: A family-owned Italianate-Victorian style inn in the heart of the Alamo Square Historic District, operating for over four decades and continuing a legacy dating to 1865.

hotels.name: Symphony Inn
hotels.description: A well-maintained budget motel in Hayes Valley, conveniently located near City Hall and the performing arts district with easy access to neighborhood restaurants.

hotels.name: Inn at the Opera
hotels.description: An intimate boutique hotel ideally located in the Performing Arts District near Hayes Valley, catering to opera, symphony, and ballet patrons.

hotels.name: Casa Loma Hotel
hotels.description: A European-style budget hotel near Hayes Valley offering affordable accommodation with easy access to public transit and the neighborhood's dining scene.

shops.name: Métier
shops.description: An intimate Hayes Valley jewelry salon specializing in one-of-a-kind estate and contemporary pieces by artists including Gabriella Kiss, Harwell Godfrey, and Gillian Conroy.

shops.name: AETHER Apparel
shops.description: A striking Hayes Valley store built from three stacked shipping containers, carrying the brand's full line of technical outerwear and travel-ready layers.

shops.name: Cotton Sheep
shops.description: A family-run Hayes Valley boutique specializing in rare Japanese denim labels like Kapital, jewelry from Masato, crafted bags from Porter, and curated home goods.

shops.name: Marine Layer
shops.description: Hayes Valley outpost of the popular SF-founded brand, offering signature soft knits, sweatshirts, and tees made from cotton-modal blends.

shops.name: Peak Design
shops.type: Camera and travel gear flagship store
shops.description: The flagship Hayes Valley store for the SF-based Peak Design, selling bags, camera straps, tripods, and everyday carry gear in a beautifully designed retail space.

shops.name: The Epicurean Trader
shops.description: A curated Hayes Valley shop stocking artisan provisions, craft beer, wine, and spirits alongside an in-house coffee bar.

shops.name: Fiddlesticks
shops.description: A cheerful Hayes Street children's boutique stocked with colorful clothing, toys, and books, blending playful design with durable quality.

shops.name: Bulo Shoes
shops.description: A well-regarded Hayes Street shoe boutique carrying a carefully edited selection of European and independent footwear brands.

shops.name: minimal

shops.description: A charming Hayes Valley boutique known for its distinctive jewelry selection and dainty accessories at accessible price points.

shops.name: Todd Snyder

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.type: Jazz and world music concert hall
artEntertainment.description: The first stand-alone structure in the US built specifically for jazz, SFJAZZ presents more than 100 concerts a year in the Robert N. Miner Auditorium and the 100-seat Joe Henderson Lab at the corner of Franklin and Fell streets.

artEntertainment.name: Madrone Art Bar
